sources.title: Outpatient treatment of COVID-19 and incidence of post-COVID-19 condition over 10 months (COVID-OUT): a multicentre, randomised, quadruple-blind, parallel-group, phase 3 trial
sources.population: Adults 30–85, overweight or obesity, acute COVID symptoms under 7 days; no known prior infection
sources.status: Private AI draft · Not appraised
sources.preview: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID after metformin began during acute infection, but this result remains provisional while an indexed correction is reconciled. The result does not establish treatment benefit for people who already have Long COVID. The long-term analysis used a selected follow-up group. Cumulative-incidence percentages are withheld because the acquired source reports conflicting control values.

review.summary: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID after metformin began during acute infection, but the result remains provisional pending correction reconciliation. Its result belongs to prevention, because treatment began before the long-term illness being counted. A reader who already has long COVID faces a different question, and this study cannot supply that answer. This unresolved source-integrity issue prevents treating the reported finding as a settled prevention conclusion. The clinical meaning depends on who entered the study, how a diagnosis was counted, and what later trials found. This draft preserves those boundaries and does not assign an evidence grade or recommend a regimen.
review.methods: The trial used masked random allocation and a factorial design, allowing metformin and matched placebo groups to contain balanced co-treatments. The long-term analysis included 1126 people, while the original randomized population was larger. Those counts answer different questions: assignment describes the trial population, whereas the long-term group describes the participants contributing to this analysis. Eligibility selected adults with overweight or obesity and a recent infection, without a known earlier infection. Our appraisal priority is therefore both internal comparison and applicability. Neither randomization nor a large initial recruitment total automatically makes the result representative of people with different clinical histories.
review.results: At day 300, the source-reported hazard ratio was 0.59 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.39 to 0.89; this estimate remains provisional while the correction is unresolved. Cumulative-incidence percentages are withheld from this summary because the acquired source contains conflicting control values. The hazard ratio is a time-to-event measure, not an event fraction computed from the enrollment total. Its reported direction favors metformin for the measured diagnosis outcome, but that direction is not an approved efficacy conclusion. Our interpretation remains narrower than a claim that every long COVID symptom was prevented. A diagnosis depends on recognition and contact with care, and the study's endpoint does not directly measure every possible symptom experience. Outcome definitions need to travel with the number whenever it is quoted.
review.limits: Long-term diagnosis was a secondary outcome added during the trial, and participation in extended follow-up was selective. The paper itself says it does not establish treatment benefit in people who already have long COVID. A correction notice is linked to the paper, but this pilot has not reconciled its exact amended text. The acquired manuscript also gives a different placebo percentage in its Discussion than in its Results. We withhold cumulative-incidence percentages and keep the reported hazard ratio provisional and publication on hold. This is a source-integrity question for the review packet, not a reason to silently choose whichever number makes the claim sound stronger.
review.sources: The original report, trial identifier NCT04510194, and linked correction remain the source trail for this draft. The source file is an HTML manuscript acquired from PMC; no PDF was downloaded or visually audited for this record. Supplemental materials and the acute-outcome companion report require further reconciliation before a complete trial-family appraisal. Funding and author disclosures are recorded separately from the result because they inform scrutiny but do not determine whether an estimate is true. The next editorial step is an exact-version source audit followed by independent human review. This preview is not that approval and should not be presented as a released appraisal.

sources.title: Metformin on the Presence of COVID-19 Symptoms 6 Months after Infection: The ACTIV-6 Randomized Clinical Trial.
authors: Accelerating COVID-19 Therapeutic Interventions and Vaccines (ACTIV)-6 Study Group and Investigators
sources.design: Quadruple-blind randomized decentralized placebo-controlled platform trial
sources.population: Outpatients at least 30 years old with acute COVID; prior infection/vaccination allowed
sources.status: Private AI draft · Not appraised
sources.preview: This randomized prevention trial did not meet its efficacy threshold for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months. The secondary clinician-diagnosis point estimate favored metformin, but its interval included no difference and does not replace the primary result. The study had few observed events and missing follow-up responses. These findings concern treatment during acute infection, not starting metformin to treat an established Long COVID illness.

review.summary: ACTIV-6 tested metformin begun during acute infection and did not meet its stated efficacy threshold for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months. The secondary participant-reported clinician-diagnosis estimate favored metformin, but its credible interval included no difference. These findings should be read together without swapping their roles. Our interpretation is that the primary result limits the strength of a broad prevention claim, while the secondary finding remains relevant to future investigation. The trial does not test whether metformin treats symptoms in someone who already has long COVID. Keeping that distinction visible makes the evidence useful even when it does not give a simple yes or no.
review.methods: The modified intention-to-treat analysis included 2983 adults from a later pandemic period, and prior infection or vaccination was common. The study compared a 14-day metformin course with matched placebo during acute illness. Its primary long-term outcome asked about symptoms on a particular follow-up day rather than accumulating all clinician diagnoses over ten months. Our reading treats this difference as part of the scientific question, not a nuisance to erase. A result can differ from an earlier trial because the people, background risk, timing, measurement, or actual treatment effect differs. This pilot does not attempt to separate those explanations quantitatively.
review.results: The adjusted difference for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at day 180 was −0.8 percentage points, with a 95% credible interval from −2.2 to 0.6. The posterior probability of benefit was 0.83, below the trial's 0.975 threshold. A negative difference favors metformin, but the interval also contains no difference and a small difference in the other direction. Our interpretation is therefore uncertainty about the size and presence of benefit under this study's model, rather than proof of equal outcomes. The secondary clinician-diagnosis estimate also had an interval including no difference and does not override the primary finding. Its intervals were not adjusted for multiple comparisons, so it needs its own cautious, outcome-specific reading.
review.limits: The day-180 symptom outcome was missing for 593 participants, and observed events were uncommon. The article reports changes to the analysis plan after the day-28 analysis, including the efficacy threshold and provisions for fewer events. These choices require protocol and statistical-plan comparison in a formal appraisal. Missing responses were handled through a model, which is more informative than pretending every missing person was symptom-free but still depends on assumptions. Tolerability was not comprehensively assessed beyond selected safety events. We therefore do not turn the paper's reassuring safety language into a general safety rating, especially for people outside its eligibility and clinical context.
review.sources: The current journal report and its NCBI identity are linked, and the earlier preprint is treated as another version of the same report rather than a separate replication. Relevant publisher HTML sections were accessible through the research tool, while direct HTML download returned an access error. A saved extraction snapshot supports the located findings; it is not a full downloaded PDF. The supplement, protocol changes, and comprehensive conflict disclosures remain review tasks. Our priority before release is to resolve those tasks and obtain human approval of the exact content version. Neither a successful import nor this written explanation is a completed risk-of-bias assessment.

sources.title: Nirmatrelvir-Ritonavir and Symptoms in Adults With Postacute Sequelae of SARS-CoV-2 Infection: The STOP-PASC Randomized Clinical Trial
sources.population: Adults with at least two moderate/severe core PASC symptoms, at least 3 months duration
sources.status: Private AI draft · Not appraised
sources.preview: A 15-day nirmatrelvir–ritonavir course did not significantly improve the selected symptom outcomes in STOP-PASC. Participants already had long COVID, so the question differed from acute treatment or prevention. Symptoms improved in both groups. The small, selected, single-center population limits broader conclusions, and later trials still require full-text reconciliation. The source includes a correction to Figure 2.

review.summary: STOP-PASC did not find a significant benefit from a 15-day nirmatrelvir–ritonavir course for its selected long COVID symptoms. The study is relevant to established illness because participants already had persistent symptoms when treatment began. Both groups improved over time, which makes the randomized comparison more informative than a before-and-after story about the active drug alone. Our interpretation is that this regimen did not demonstrate the expected advantage in the enrolled population. The finding does not settle every antiviral, duration, symptom subtype, or possible mechanism. It does challenge a claim that improvement after taking this treatment, by itself, proves a drug effect.
review.methods: Researchers randomized 155 adults at Stanford to nirmatrelvir plus ritonavir or placebo plus ritonavir. The primary assessment pooled severity across six core symptom groups at ten weeks. Enrollment stopped early after the prespecified futility criterion was reached. This design matters because the control was not simply an inert substitute for every component of the active combination. Our reading keeps the exact comparator in every interpretation. The trial also selected participants according to clinical and medication criteria, so its experience should not be extended to excluded people without further evidence. Randomization supports comparison within the trial; it does not eliminate every question about applicability.
review.results: The primary pooled symptom comparison did not show a significant between-group difference. As an illustrative secondary outcome, the adjusted difference in PROMIS fatigue change was 0.38 points, with a 95% confidence interval from −2.40 to 3.15. Fatigue improved within both groups, but that is not the same as evidence that the active treatment caused greater improvement. Our interpretation gives priority to the comparison the trial was designed to make. The interval also prevents a claim that an exact zero effect has been established. Secondary and exploratory findings need caution because multiple comparisons can generate apparently interesting differences even without a reproducible treatment advantage.
review.limits: This was a single-center study, with a smaller sample than planned and a mostly vaccinated population with prolonged symptoms. Taste disturbance differed between groups and could have affected masking of self-reported outcomes. Adverse events and treatment discontinuations were recorded, but a modest trial cannot provide a complete picture of rare harms or risks in excluded patients. Our review therefore keeps harms visible alongside the absence of demonstrated benefit. It also separates study exclusions from medical contraindications: the latter require current product-specific authoritative information and qualified clinical interpretation. There is no dosing recommendation in this review and no inference that a longer course would work.
review.sources: The PMC article includes a correction dated July 22, 2024, concerning the placement of dashed lines in Figure 2. We retain that notice with the paper rather than treating the corrected figure as a new study. The source was acquired as HTML; its tables were read as text, and PDF visual verification remains pending. Pfizer funded the trial and collaborated on its design, execution, and manuscript review, with disclosures recorded in the evidence data. RECOVER-VITAL is a later nirmatrelvir–ritonavir trial represented by an acquired abstract in this collection. Its full-text reconciliation remains incomplete. This draft is an original reading aid awaiting source audit and human editorial approval, not a released clinical recommendation.

sources.correction: July 22 2024 correction repositions dashed lines in Figure 2. Current PMC article explicitly includes correction.

recordSections.title: Source summary

recordSections.label: Methods
recordSections.title: Design and population
recordSections.paragraph: Prospective randomized double-blind placebo-controlled adjunctive pilot trial; per-protocol analysis. Adults aged at least 50 years with Parkinson's disease receiving levodopa/carbidopa; diabetes and several other conditions excluded; single center in Egypt. 60 randomized, 30 per arm. Results analyzed 27 metformin and 25 control after 3 and 5 withdrawals respectively (pp3–6). Metformin 500 mg twice daily is dose, not sample size.

recordSections.label: Results
recordSections.title: Extracted outcomes
recordSections.paragraph: Primary UPDRS total at 3 months: Metformin median (IQR) 152 (129–166) at baseline and 128 (98–151) after treatment; control 141 (115–164) and 139 (101–151.5). Between-group post-treatment P=0.515, rank-biserial r=0.106. Within-metformin P=0.001 is not evidence of superiority to control. (PDF p6 Table2; p7 Results). Clinical subscores: All between-group post-treatment tests nonsignificant: mentation/behavior/mood P=0.195, activities of daily living P=0.441, motor examination P=0.426, therapy complications P=0.705, Schwab/England P=0.137, modified Hoehn/Yahr P=0.082. (PDF p6 Table2). Biomarkers after 3 months: Between-group differences were reported for alpha-synuclein, BDNF, HMGB-1 and TLR4 (PDF p7 Table3). Units for all biomarker estimates are not fully represented in the accepted extraction, so their numerical magnitudes are withheld here. Biomarker differences do not establish clinical superiority. Reported adverse effects: Metformin/control counts: nausea 6/5, diarrhea 4/2, vomiting 5/3, hypotension 9/5, delusions 5/3, abdominal pain 8/5, with arm denominators 27/25. All reported comparisons P>0.05; this small study does not establish equivalent safety. (PDF p8 Table4).

recordSections.label: Limits
recordSections.title: Stated limitations
recordSections.paragraph: Short duration, small sample, one metformin dose, single center/Middle East population; metabolic rate and dietary habits not measured/controlled; further biomarker and vitamin B12/lipid/glucose assessment desirable (pp8–9).

recordSections.title: Extracted outcomes
recordSections.paragraph: Between-group metabolite differences at week24: Baseline-adjusted least-square mean differences (95% CI), μg/mL: oxaloacetic acid0.87(0.61,1.13); citric acid4.40(3.35,5.45); isocitric acid0.50(0.37,0.63); alpha-ketoglutaric acid0.56(0.41,0.71); succinic acid5.77(4.03,7.51); fumaric acid0.45(0.28,0.63); malic acid0.27(0.19,0.35); lactic acid−148.09(−184.61,−111.57); pyruvic acid−38.17(−47.18,−29.17); all P<0.001. (PDF p8 Table3 week24). Hippocampal functional connectivity: Left caudal hippocampus/right medio-ventral occipital cortex difference−0.334 at week12; right caudal hippocampus/right middle frontal gyrus difference0.284 at week24; both P<0.001. (PDF p7 Results; Fig1 p5). Exploratory cognition correlations: Week12 working-memory change correlated with alpha-ketoglutaric acid r=0.34, succinic acid r=0.36, lactic acid r=0.34 (P<0.05); week24 verbal learning negatively correlated with alpha-ketoglutaric acid r=−0.49 and fumaric acid r=−0.48 (P<0.01). These are associations, not proof of mediation. (PDF p7 Results; Fig2 p8). Treatment interaction and null findings: Only the week12 succinic-acid change×treatment interaction for week24 working memory reached P=0.0193; other tested interactive effects were not statistically significant. Negative relationship for the significant interaction discussed. Current numerical cognitive between-arm efficacy estimate NOT IN CORPUS; prior report cited. (PDF pp8,10; p7 opening cognition paragraph).

recordSections.label: Limits
recordSections.title: Stated limitations
recordSections.paragraph: Small sample, incomplete blood/MRI time points, potential confounding and medication-adherence bias, short follow-up, mechanism incompletely explored (pp10–11). sources.title: Itraconazole, a commonly used anti-fungal that inhibits Hedgehog pathway activity and cancer growth
sources.population: Shh-Light2/NIH-3T3 reporter cells, pathway-mutant cells and mouse tumor allografts
sources.status: Full text inspected · Review pending
sources.preview: Itraconazole suppressed Hedgehog signaling in reporter and tumor models, with experiments locating its action near Smoothened. Fluconazole did not share this activity in the tested assay.
sources.decisiveLimit: Model-specific pathway inhibition is not a cancer-treatment outcome. Serum conditions materially changed potency.

locators.section: Results and Discussion; Figures 1B,D, 2D,E and 4A–E; Experimental Procedures: Hh pathway activity assays
locators.basis: Original full-text methods and results inspected; dedicated appraisal pending.

sources.title: Cholesterol trafficking is required for mTOR activation in endothelial cells
sources.population: Human umbilical-vein endothelial cells (HUVECs)
sources.status: Full text inspected · Review pending
sources.preview: Endothelial-cell experiments linked blocked intracellular cholesterol transport to reduced mTOR signaling and proliferation. Rescue experiments strengthened the proposed connection.
sources.decisiveLimit: Endothelial-cell assays do not establish tumor oxygenation, survival benefit or patient exposure at the target.

locators.section: Results: Itraconazole Inhibits Cholesterol Trafficking; Proper Cholesterol Trafficking Is Essential; Figures 3–5; Materials and Methods
locators.basis: Original full-text methods and results inspected; dedicated appraisal pending.

sources.title: Simultaneous Targeting of NPC1 and VDAC1 by Itraconazole Leads to Synergistic Inhibition of mTOR Signaling and Angiogenesis
sources.population: HEK293T and A549 target-binding assays; HUVEC signaling and tube formation
sources.status: Full text inspected · Review pending
sources.preview: Live-cell binding experiments identified NPC1 as an itraconazole target. The report linked cholesterol trafficking and a parallel AMPK pathway to suppression of endothelial growth.
sources.decisiveLimit: Cell and binding studies; clinical benefit was not tested. Supplementary methods and raw images need separate appraisal.

locators.section: Results: Itraconazole Binds Directly to NPC1 (Figure 2); AMPK Activation and NPC Induction (Figures 4–5); main-text assay descriptions

sources.title: Fenbendazole acts as a moderate microtubule destabilizing agent and causes cancer cell death by modulating multiple cellular pathways
sources.population: Human lung-cancer cell lines, purified bovine tubulin and A549 mouse xenografts
sources.status: Full text inspected · Review pending
sources.preview: Fenbendazole altered microtubules, cell division and metabolic readouts in lung-cancer models. These experiments explain a research rationale without establishing treatment benefit in people.
sources.decisiveLimit: No human cancer trial or safe human anticancer exposure was established. Laboratory selectivity is not clinical safety.

locators.section: Results: FZ destabilizes tubulin network; FZ treatment results in early G2/M block; Figures 1, 3–8; Methods: tubulin assay and nude mice
locators.basis: Original full-text methods and results inspected; dedicated appraisal pending.

sources.title: Effects of Azole Antifungal Drugs on the Transition from Yeast Cells to Hyphae in Susceptible and Resistant Isolates of the Pathogenic Yeast Candida albicans
sources.population: Susceptible and resistant clinical Candida albicans isolates
sources.status: Full text inspected · Review pending
sources.preview: Fluconazole inhibited hyphal development in susceptible Candida isolates under specified laboratory conditions. Resistant isolates could retain this invasive-growth trait.
sources.decisiveLimit: Hyphal morphology is not direct measurement of human tissue invasion; results depended on strain, medium and exposure timing.

locators.section: Materials and Methods: hyphal induction; Results: Fluconazole inhibits hyphal formation; Figures 1–5; Discussion
locators.basis: Original full-text methods and results inspected; dedicated appraisal pending.

sources.title: Expression of fluconazole resistance-associated genes in biofilm from 23 clinical isolates of Candida albicans
sources.population: 23 clinical Candida albicans isolates; eight selected for gene-expression measurements
sources.status: Full text inspected · Review pending
sources.preview: Clinical Candida isolates became less susceptible to fluconazole as laboratory biofilms matured. The experiment does not support describing fluconazole as a general biofilm-destroying drug.
sources.decisiveLimit: Plate biofilms and a nonstandardized biofilm inoculum limit clinical interpretation; prevention is distinct from eradication.

locators.section: Methods: Antifungal susceptibility testing and gene expression; Results: Table 2 and Figures 2–4; Discussion
locators.basis: Original full-text methods and results inspected; dedicated appraisal pending.

guides.title: Metformin and long COVID prevention
guides.description: What the metformin trials found about later Long COVID after treatment during acute infection.

sections.label: Answer
sections.title: What did the prevention trials find?
sections.paragraph: COVID-OUT reported a lower hazard of later clinician-diagnosed Long COVID, although an indexed correction and conflicting cumulative-incidence values complicate interpretation. ACTIV-6 did not meet its efficacy threshold for its primary long-term symptom outcome.

sections.label: Context
sections.title: When treatment began
sections.paragraph: Both studies began treatment during acute COVID-19. They address prevention of later illness; the separate Korean trial tested treatment after Long COVID symptoms were already established.

sentences.text: Both studies began treatment during acute COVID-19. They address prevention of later illness; the separate Korean trial tested treatment after Long COVID symptoms were already established.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: Symptoms and diagnosis were different outcomes
sections.paragraph: In ACTIV-6, the adjusted risk difference for symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months was −0.8 percentage points, with a 95% credible interval of −2.2 to 0.6. The secondary clinician-diagnosis estimate was −0.7 percentage points, with an interval of −1.5 to 0.1. Both intervals included no difference.

guides.title: Prevention versus treatment
guides.description: How timing, participants and outcomes explain differences between Long COVID trials.

sections.label: Question
sections.title: Start with the disease stage
sections.paragraph: A repurposing claim becomes clearer when it states when treatment begins and what outcome it aims to change. The metformin prevention trials began during acute infection, while the Korean metformin trial and STOP-PASC enrolled people with established symptoms. These are different clinical questions even when the medicine or disease name overlaps. This guide uses that contrast to help readers locate the right evidence, rather than treating every mention of long COVID as the same research problem.

guides.title: Metformin
guides.description: How metformin works, its investigated benefits across infections, cancer, neurological conditions and physical function, and its safety.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: What is metformin?
sections.paragraph: Metformin is an oral glucose-lowering medicine in the biguanide class. In the United States, immediate-release metformin tablets are approved alongside diet and exercise for type 2 diabetes in adults and children aged 10 years and older. It reduces the liver’s glucose production and improves the body’s response to insulin; those established uses are distinct from the repurposing investigations discussed here. Researchers are studying whether its effects on metabolism, cellular energy sensing and inflammatory pathways can help in acute COVID-19 and Long COVID, Parkinson’s disease, cognition in schizophrenia, and age-related loss of muscle function. Cancer research includes trials in prostate, lung, breast and pancreatic cancer, studies of recurrent colorectal adenomas after polyp removal, and laboratory work in multiple myeloma. The findings vary by condition and outcome: promising biological effects have often failed to translate into clinical benefit, and preventing a condition, treating established disease and changing a laboratory marker are different questions.

The findings vary by condition and outcome: promising biological effects have often failed to translate into clinical benefit, and preventing a condition, treating established disease and changing a laboratory marker are different questions.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: The benefits being investigated include reducing Long COVID risk, improving cognition in schizophrenia, preserving physical function in older adults and improving Parkinson’s symptoms. A small schizophrenia trial reported improved cognitive-test scores with metformin, while the Parkinson’s pilot and the MET-PREVENT sarcopenia trial did not demonstrate improvements in their main clinical outcomes. For Long COVID, COVID-OUT reported a prevention signal, although a correction notice and inconsistent control percentages complicate interpretation; ACTIV-6 did not meet its primary efficacy threshold, and a separate trial found no improved recovery after symptoms were established. Cancer trials have generally not demonstrated the hoped-for treatment benefits; a separate colorectal study found fewer recurrent adenomas after polyp removal, which is a prevention outcome.

questions.question: Does metformin improve symptoms of Parkinson’s disease?
questions.answer: A three-month pilot randomized 60 people to metformin or placebo alongside levodopa/carbidopa. Clinical scores improved within the metformin group, but the comparison between groups did not show a statistically significant benefit on the total Unified Parkinson’s Disease Rating Scale. The trial was small, used a per-protocol analysis and was too short to establish whether metformin slows disease progression.

The trial was small, used a per-protocol analysis and was too short to establish whether metformin slows disease progression.

questions.question: What has the schizophrenia research found about cognition?
questions.answer: In a 72-person open-label randomized trial, adding metformin to antipsychotic treatment improved the composite cognitive-test score by an estimated 3.43 points more than antipsychotics alone after 24 weeks (95% CI 1.83–5.02). The participants were predominantly young adults, 59 completed follow-up, and the study lacked a placebo group; larger blinded studies are needed to confirm the size and practical importance of this effect. A later analysis of the same trial linked changes in metabolites and hippocampal connectivity with cognitive changes.

questions.question: Does metformin improve muscle strength or physical function?
questions.answer: The 2025 MET-PREVENT trial randomized 72 older adults with probable sarcopenia and prefrailty or frailty to metformin or placebo for four months. It found no walking-speed benefit: the adjusted difference was 0.001 m/s (95% CI −0.06 to 0.06), and metformin was poorly tolerated in this population. The 2023 review described inconsistent results: some research suggested faster walking, but strength outcomes were not consistently improved and exercise adaptations could be reduced. In the MASTERS trial, adding metformin to resistance training reduced muscle growth in healthy older adults; the difference in strength gains was not statistically significant.

questions.question: Does taking metformin during COVID-19 prevent Long COVID?
questions.answer: COVID-OUT reported fewer later clinician-diagnosed cases when treatment began during acute infection, but the estimate remains provisional because the report contains inconsistent control percentages and has a published correction. ACTIV-6 examined symptoms attributed to COVID-19 or death at six months and did not meet its prespecified threshold for benefit. The trials enrolled different populations and used different outcomes, leaving uncertainty about how much prevention benefit metformin provides.

questions.question: Does metformin help when Long COVID is already established?
questions.answer: A randomized South Korean trial did not find improved recovery after a two-week course of metformin in people with persistent symptoms. That result concerns the population and short treatment course tested; it does not establish the effect of longer courses or treatment in every Long COVID subgroup. A separate metformin-and-fluvoxamine fatigue report was retracted and republished; its original findings cannot serve as reliable evidence of metformin benefit.

sections.paragraph: Long COVID can involve persistent or recurring fatigue, problems with thinking, breathlessness and worsening symptoms after physical or mental effort. Symptoms can affect several body systems and continue for months or years. Repurposing studies ask two different questions: whether treatment during acute infection reduces later illness, and whether treatment helps people who already have persistent symptoms.

sections.paragraph: Epithelial ovarian, fallopian-tube and primary peritoneal cancers arise in closely related tissues and are treated using overlapping approaches. Histological subtype, stage and prior response to platinum chemotherapy influence the treatment question. Repurposing research includes itraconazole in recurrent ovarian clear cell carcinoma, a specific subtype that can respond poorly to cytotoxic treatment.

guides.title: Glioblastoma

sections.paragraph: Glioblastoma is an aggressive glioma that infiltrates brain tissue. Treatment commonly combines surgery where feasible with radiation and chemotherapy, but infiltration makes complete removal difficult. Mebendazole, an antiparasitic medicine, has been investigated as an addition to temozolomide in newly diagnosed high-grade gliomas.

guides.title: Fibromyalgia
guides.description: Low-dose naltrexone in fibromyalgia: the pain-processing rationale and the results of a larger placebo-controlled trial.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Fibromyalgia causes widespread pain and tenderness, often with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and difficulty thinking clearly. Research points to altered pain processing rather than a single damaged joint or muscle. Low-dose naltrexone has been studied as a way to change central pain modulation.

sentences.text: Fibromyalgia causes widespread pain and tenderness, often with fatigue, unrefreshing sleep and difficulty thinking clearly. Research points to altered pain processing rather than a single damaged joint or muscle.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: In a 2024 trial of 99 women, naltrexone did not produce superior pain relief over placebo after 12 weeks. The between-group pain difference was −0.34 points on an 11-point scale, with a 95% confidence interval from −0.95 to 0.27. The exploratory report did not find an association between changes in conditioned pain modulation and improvement in clinical pain. Part of the group difference reflected worsening in the placebo group. Confidence that this isolated laboratory result demonstrates meaningful symptom benefit is Low: the authors considered it potentially spurious, and several exploratory outcomes were tested without a dedicated sample-size calculation.

sections.paragraph: The pain trial was randomized and double-blind. Its estimate allows both a modest pain benefit and no benefit, but does not support the proposed average superiority over placebo. A later report examined exploratory pain-processing and muscle-endurance outcomes from the same FINAL trial. It is not an independent second treatment trial. The complete-case analysis included 45 naltrexone and 47 placebo participants. Only conditioned pain modulation differed significantly among the five exploratory outcomes: the between-group change was 2.0 kPa, with a 95% confidence interval of 0.4 to 3.7 kPa. That laboratory finding should be read alongside the trial's clinical pain result, rather than substituted for it.

guides.title: Myalgic encephalomyelitis/chronic fatigue syndrome
guides.description: ME/CFS repurposing evidence: patient-derived immune-cell findings, anecdotal naltrexone responses and unresolved clinical questions.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: ME/CFS is a disabling multisystem illness marked by reduced ability to carry out usual activities, unrefreshing sleep and post-exertional malaise. Physical or mental effort can cause a delayed worsening of symptoms. Naltrexone research has examined altered signaling in natural-killer immune cells as one possible treatment target.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low for symptom benefit. The TRPM3 study examined natural-killer cells from nine people with ME/CFS already taking naltrexone and nine healthy controls. Channel currents resembled those in healthy-control cells. There was no randomized treated-versus-untreated ME/CFS comparison measuring recovery, daily function or post-exertional malaise. Clinical evidence: Low. Three published patient-compiled case histories described variable symptom changes during naltrexone use. One reported better pain and sleep without improved function. Self-selection, retrospective reporting, other treatments and illness fluctuation prevent a causal response estimate; these cases do not establish a validated ME/CFS dose.

This product warning is separate from the unproven benefits and dosing of low-dose treatment for ME/CFS.

sections.paragraph: The neurological series included cases associated with medication effects and underlying nerve or spinal pathology. A medicine history and evaluation of accompanying neurological symptoms can therefore change the explanation of symptoms.

sentences.text: The neurological series included cases associated with medication effects and underlying nerve or spinal pathology. A medicine history and evaluation of accompanying neurological symptoms can therefore change the explanation of symptoms.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: PGAD and CSBD should be distinguished in research comparisons: one centers on unwanted physical sensation, the other on impaired control of behavior. Combining them would obscure whether a treatment helps the symptom that brought a person to care.

sentences.text: PGAD and CSBD should be distinguished in research comparisons: one centers on unwanted physical sensation, the other on impaired control of behavior. Combining them would obscure whether a treatment helps the symptom that brought a person to care.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The neurological case series and the iPGAD case-control study investigate causes and clinical features. Neither design supplies a randomized estimate of naltrexone’s effect on PGAD symptoms.

sentences.text: The neurological case series and the iPGAD case-control study investigate causes and clinical features. Neither design supplies a randomized estimate of naltrexone’s effect on PGAD symptoms.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The CSBD page covers naltrexone research on repetitive behavior, making the difference in symptom targets explicit.

sentences.text: The CSBD page covers naltrexone research on repetitive behavior, making the difference in symptom targets explicit.

faqs.question: Can unwanted genital sensations occur without wanting sexual activity?
faqs.answer: Yes. Lack of corresponding sexual desire is a defining feature of the symptoms investigated in the iPGAD study.

sentences.text: Yes. Lack of corresponding sexual desire is a defining feature of the symptoms investigated in the iPGAD study.

guides.title: Treatment-resistant depression
guides.description: Pramipexole augmentation for treatment-resistant depression, including the dopamine rationale and randomized trial evidence.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Treatment-resistant depression describes continuing depressive illness despite adequate treatment attempts. Its symptoms can include loss of pleasure, motivation and daily function as well as persistent low mood. Pramipexole, originally used for movement disorders, has been studied as an addition to existing antidepressants.

sentences.text: Treatment-resistant depression describes continuing depressive illness despite adequate treatment attempts. Its symptoms can include loss of pleasure, motivation and daily function as well as persistent low mood.
Pramipexole, originally used for movement disorders, has been studied as an addition to existing antidepressants.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The 2025 PAX-D trial found a greater reduction in depressive symptoms with pramipexole augmentation than placebo at 12 weeks. The benefit came with adverse effects, making both symptom change and tolerability relevant.

sentences.text: The 2025 PAX-D trial found a greater reduction in depressive symptoms with pramipexole augmentation than placebo at 12 weeks. The benefit came with adverse effects, making both symptom change and tolerability relevant.

questions.question: Was pramipexole tested as a replacement for antidepressants?
questions.answer: No. PAX-D tested it as an add-on in treatment-resistant unipolar depression. Its result does not directly answer whether pramipexole alone is effective or whether the same balance applies to bipolar depression.

sentences.text: No. PAX-D tested it as an add-on in treatment-resistant unipolar depression. Its result does not directly answer whether pramipexole alone is effective or whether the same balance applies to bipolar depression.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Treatment stopped because of adverse events in 20% with pramipexole versus 5% with placebo. Reported effects included nausea, headache, disturbed sleep and somnolence.

sentences.text: Treatment stopped because of adverse events in 20% with pramipexole versus 5% with placebo. Reported effects included nausea, headache, disturbed sleep and somnolence.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: PAX-D provides a placebo comparison for an augmentation strategy in unipolar depression. It was not a head-to-head comparison with ketamine, electroconvulsive therapy or another augmentation medicine.

sentences.text: PAX-D provides a placebo comparison for an augmentation strategy in unipolar depression. It was not a head-to-head comparison with ketamine, electroconvulsive therapy or another augmentation medicine.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The primary PAX-D outcome was depressive-symptom change at 12 weeks. The adjusted between-group difference was −3.91 QIDS-SR points (95% CI −5.37 to −2.45).

sentences.text: The primary PAX-D outcome was depressive-symptom change at 12 weeks. The adjusted between-group difference was −3.91 QIDS-SR points (95% CI −5.37 to −2.45).

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The pramipexole profile explains dopamine-receptor activity and the distinction between its movement-disorder use and antidepressant augmentation.

sentences.text: The pramipexole profile explains dopamine-receptor activity and the distinction between its movement-disorder use and antidepressant augmentation.

faqs.question: Is loss of pleasure relevant to depression research?
faqs.answer: Yes. Loss of interest or enjoyment is a core depressive symptom, and dopamine-focused research has specifically examined reward and motivation.

sentences.text: Yes. Loss of interest or enjoyment is a core depressive symptom, and dopamine-focused research has specifically examined reward and motivation.

guides.scope: Pramipexole augmentation for treatment-resistant depression, including the dopamine rationale and randomized trial evidence.

guides.title: Periodontitis
guides.description: Doxycycline as a periodontal host-response treatment, and how its benefit differs from dental cleaning or antibiotic dosing.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Periodontitis involves inflammation and destruction of the tissues and bone that support teeth. Bacterial plaque initiates the problem, while the body’s inflammatory response contributes to tissue damage. Doxycycline has been repurposed at subantimicrobial exposure to inhibit tissue-degrading enzymes, alongside mechanical periodontal treatment.

sentences.text: Periodontitis involves inflammation and destruction of the tissues and bone that support teeth. Bacterial plaque initiates the problem, while the body’s inflammatory response contributes to tissue damage.
Doxycycline has been repurposed at subantimicrobial exposure to inhibit tissue-degrading enzymes, alongside mechanical periodontal treatment.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: A multicenter trial found greater improvements in attachment level and periodontal pocket depth when subantimicrobial-dose doxycycline was added to scaling and root planing than with cleaning plus placebo.

sentences.text: A multicenter trial found greater improvements in attachment level and periodontal pocket depth when subantimicrobial-dose doxycycline was added to scaling and root planing than with cleaning plus placebo.

questions.question: Does doxycycline replace scaling and root planing?
questions.answer: No. The trial tested an adjunct to mechanical treatment. Its result concerns the additional effect of the medicine when both groups received periodontal cleaning.

sentences.text: No. The trial tested an adjunct to mechanical treatment. Its result concerns the additional effect of the medicine when both groups received periodontal cleaning.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: The periodontal trial followed patients receiving the medicine alongside dental treatment. Smoking and uncontrolled local plaque remain important influences on healing and disease progression, regardless of the adjunct chosen.

sentences.text: The periodontal trial followed patients receiving the medicine alongside dental treatment. Smoking and uncontrolled local plaque remain important influences on healing and disease progression, regardless of the adjunct chosen.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Attachment gain and pocket-depth change are periodontal outcomes; they are not interchangeable with immediate pain relief or removal of plaque. The useful comparison is the same dental care with or without the adjunct.

sentences.text: Attachment gain and pocket-depth change are periodontal outcomes; they are not interchangeable with immediate pain relief or removal of plaque. The useful comparison is the same dental care with or without the adjunct.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The multicenter study analyzed 209 patients over nine months. Clinical attachment level and probing depth measure the supporting tissues and periodontal pockets, not eradication of all oral bacteria.

sentences.text: The multicenter study analyzed 209 patients over nine months. Clinical attachment level and probing depth measure the supporting tissues and periodontal pockets, not eradication of all oral bacteria.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The doxycycline profile follows its host-enzyme action, separate from its antibacterial uses.

sentences.text: The doxycycline profile follows its host-enzyme action, separate from its antibacterial uses.

faqs.question: Can periodontitis affect tooth support?
faqs.answer: Yes. The disease damages the tissues and bone that hold teeth in place. That is why attachment level and pocket depth are relevant treatment measurements.

sentences.text: Yes. The disease damages the tissues and bone that hold teeth in place. That is why attachment level and pocket depth are relevant treatment measurements.

guides.scope: Doxycycline as a periodontal host-response treatment, and how its benefit differs from dental cleaning or antibiotic dosing.

guides.title: Crohn disease
guides.description: How molecular profiles in Crohn’s disease are being used to identify new treatment candidates.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Crohn’s disease causes chronic inflammation in the digestive tract, with symptoms such as diarrhea, abdominal pain and weight loss. Treatment aims to control inflammation and maintain remission.

sentences.text: Crohn’s disease causes chronic inflammation in the digestive tract, with symptoms such as diarrhea, abdominal pain and weight loss. Treatment aims to control inflammation and maintain remission.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Repurposing research has used gene-expression patterns from people whose Crohn’s disease did not respond to anti-TNF treatment to nominate vorinostat and clomipramine. These are computational candidates; the analysis did not test symptom improvement or remission after taking either drug.

sentences.text: Repurposing research has used gene-expression patterns from people whose Crohn’s disease did not respond to anti-TNF treatment to nominate vorinostat and clomipramine. These are computational candidates; the analysis did not test symptom improvement or remission after taking either drug.

questions.question: What benefit was actually investigated?
questions.answer: The study looked for drugs that might reverse abnormal gene-expression patterns in two patient clusters. It identified candidates for experimental testing, rather than measuring a clinical treatment effect.

sentences.text: The study looked for drugs that might reverse abnormal gene-expression patterns in two patient clusters. It identified candidates for experimental testing, rather than measuring a clinical treatment effect.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: The computational study provides no Crohn’s-specific tolerability results for these candidates. Established care is selected according to disease location, activity, complications and response to previous treatment.

sentences.text: The computational study provides no Crohn’s-specific tolerability results for these candidates. Established care is selected according to disease location, activity, complications and response to previous treatment.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Vorinostat and clomipramine were nominated for different molecular clusters. The study did not compare them with one another or with an effective Crohn’s therapy.

sentences.text: Vorinostat and clomipramine were nominated for different molecular clusters. The study did not compare them with one another or with an effective Crohn’s therapy.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The Crohn’s analysis used existing transcriptomic data and drug-expression signatures. A candidate’s computational match provides no estimate of remission rate or risk of surgery.

sentences.text: The Crohn’s analysis used existing transcriptomic data and drug-expression signatures. A candidate’s computational match provides no estimate of remission rate or risk of surgery.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: Vorinostat and clomipramine were nominated for different molecular clusters in the same Crohn’s analysis.

sentences.text: Vorinostat and clomipramine were nominated for different molecular clusters in the same Crohn’s analysis.

faqs.question: Is Crohn’s disease confined to the colon?
faqs.answer: No. Crohn’s can affect different parts of the digestive tract. Location and complications influence treatment and the meaning of a study population.

sentences.text: No. Crohn’s can affect different parts of the digestive tract. Location and complications influence treatment and the meaning of a study population.

guides.scope: How molecular profiles in Crohn’s disease are being used to identify new treatment candidates.

guides.title: Head and neck squamous cell carcinoma
guides.description: Valproic acid investigations in head and neck squamous cell cancer, including the toxicity that limited clinical testing.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Head and neck squamous cell cancers arise in the surface lining of sites such as the mouth, throat and larynx. Tobacco, alcohol and, for some sites, high-risk HPV infection contribute to risk.

sentences.text: Head and neck squamous cell cancers arise in the surface lining of sites such as the mouth, throat and larynx. Tobacco, alcohol and, for some sites, high-risk HPV infection contribute to risk.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Valproic acid was investigated as an addition to cisplatin-based chemoradiation. Although tumor responses occurred, unacceptable toxicity limited this combination study.

sentences.text: Valproic acid was investigated as an addition to cisplatin-based chemoradiation. Although tumor responses occurred, unacceptable toxicity limited this combination study.

questions.question: Did adding valproic acid establish a better treatment?
questions.answer: No comparative improvement was established. The phase II study was curtailed because toxicity, particularly bone-marrow toxicity and infection, made the regimen difficult to deliver.

sentences.text: No comparative improvement was established. The phase II study was curtailed because toxicity, particularly bone-marrow toxicity and infection, made the regimen difficult to deliver.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Marrow suppression and infections were central safety problems in the combination study. Safety observed when valproic acid is used for another indication cannot substitute for safety of this chemotherapy combination.

sentences.text: Marrow suppression and infections were central safety problems in the combination study. Safety observed when valproic acid is used for another indication cannot substitute for safety of this chemotherapy combination.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: This investigation concerns adding valproic acid to cisplatin and radiation; it does not show that valproic acid can replace either treatment.

sentences.text: This investigation concerns adding valproic acid to cisplatin and radiation; it does not show that valproic acid can replace either treatment.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: The clinical combination study could not establish a favorable benefit–harm balance because toxicity constrained delivery. The earlier cell findings answer sensitivity questions, not survival.

sentences.text: The clinical combination study could not establish a favorable benefit–harm balance because toxicity constrained delivery. The earlier cell findings answer sensitivity questions, not survival.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The valproic acid profile and AML page cover related gene-regulation hypotheses tested in different cancer settings.

sentences.text: The valproic acid profile and AML page cover related gene-regulation hypotheses tested in different cancer settings.

faqs.question: Are all head and neck tumors the same disease?
faqs.answer: No. Site, cell type and risk factors differ. Most cancers in this group arise in the squamous lining, but an intervention studied in one setting does not cover every head and neck tumor.

sentences.text: No. Site, cell type and risk factors differ. Most cancers in this group arise in the squamous lining, but an intervention studied in one setting does not cover every head and neck tumor.

guides.scope: Valproic acid investigations in head and neck squamous cell cancer, including the toxicity that limited clinical testing.

guides.title: Prostate cancer
guides.description: Itraconazole research in advanced prostate cancer, with separate PSA and disease-progression outcomes.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Prostate cancer begins in the prostate gland. The itraconazole investigation focused on metastatic cancer progressing despite testosterone-lowering treatment, a specific advanced-disease setting.

sentences.text: Prostate cancer begins in the prostate gland. The itraconazole investigation focused on metastatic cancer progressing despite testosterone-lowering treatment, a specific advanced-disease setting.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: A 46-man study found modest activity at the higher itraconazole dose. It compared two dose groups without a standard-treatment control, so it cannot show superiority to established prostate-cancer therapy.

sentences.text: A 46-man study found modest activity at the higher itraconazole dose. It compared two dose groups without a standard-treatment control, so it cannot show superiority to established prostate-cancer therapy.

questions.question: What did the higher-dose group achieve?
questions.answer: At 24 weeks, 48% had no PSA progression; median progression-free survival was 35.9 weeks. The lower-dose group closed early for insufficient activity.

sentences.text: At 24 weeks, 48% had no PSA progression; median progression-free survival was 35.9 weeks. The lower-dose group closed early for insufficient activity.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Reported adverse effects included fatigue, nausea, rash and a combination of low potassium, high blood pressure and edema.

sentences.text: Reported adverse effects included fatigue, nausea, rash and a combination of low potassium, high blood pressure and edema.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: The trial compared dose schedules, not itraconazole against an androgen-receptor treatment or chemotherapy. PSA control and progression-free survival are also distinct from a demonstrated survival benefit.

sentences.text: The trial compared dose schedules, not itraconazole against an androgen-receptor treatment or chemotherapy. PSA control and progression-free survival are also distinct from a demonstrated survival benefit.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Randomization assigned itraconazole doses; the study was explicitly noncomparative. With 29 men at the higher dose and 17 at the lower dose, estimates are imprecise.

sentences.text: Randomization assigned itraconazole doses; the study was explicitly noncomparative. With 29 men at the higher dose and 17 at the lower dose, estimates are imprecise.

sections.paragraph: The basal cell carcinoma page examines Hedgehog signaling in another itraconazole study, with different tumor biology and outcomes.

sentences.text: The basal cell carcinoma page examines Hedgehog signaling in another itraconazole study, with different tumor biology and outcomes.

faqs.question: What is the prostate?
faqs.answer: It is a gland in the male reproductive system that contributes fluid to semen. A prostate cancer study’s stage and spread are separate from that organ-level definition.

sentences.text: It is a gland in the male reproductive system that contributes fluid to semen. A prostate cancer study’s stage and spread are separate from that organ-level definition.

guides.title: Non-small-cell lung cancer
guides.description: Itraconazole added to pemetrexed in a small trial of advanced nonsquamous lung cancer.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Non-small cell lung cancer includes several types, particularly adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. The pemetrexed–itraconazole trial enrolled the nonsquamous subgroup with metastatic disease.

sentences.text: Non-small cell lung cancer includes several types, particularly adenocarcinoma and squamous cell carcinoma. The pemetrexed–itraconazole trial enrolled the nonsquamous subgroup with metastatic disease.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: Adding itraconazole to pemetrexed produced encouraging survival estimates in a trial that enrolled only 23 people before stopping early. The small sample makes those estimates uncertain.

sentences.text: Adding itraconazole to pemetrexed produced encouraging survival estimates in a trial that enrolled only 23 people before stopping early. The small sample makes those estimates uncertain.

questions.question: What happened to progression-free survival?
questions.answer: Median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with the combination and 2.8 months with pemetrexed alone; the difference did not reach conventional statistical significance (P=0.089).

sentences.text: Median progression-free survival was 5.5 months with the combination and 2.8 months with pemetrexed alone; the difference did not reach conventional statistical significance (P=0.089).

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: The study’s small enrollment limits detection of uncommon harms from adding itraconazole to chemotherapy.

sentences.text: The study’s small enrollment limits detection of uncommon harms from adding itraconazole to chemotherapy.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: Median overall survival was 32 versus 8 months, but this was a small, prematurely closed phase II study. It did not compare the combination with modern molecularly targeted or immunotherapy regimens.

sentences.text: Median overall survival was 32 versus 8 months, but this was a small, prematurely closed phase II study. It did not compare the combination with modern molecularly targeted or immunotherapy regimens.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Early closure followed changing use of pemetrexed in lung-cancer care. With only 23 participants, the trial was too small for stable efficacy estimates.

sentences.text: Early closure followed changing use of pemetrexed in lung-cancer care. With only 23 participants, the trial was too small for stable efficacy estimates.

sections.label: Connections
sections.paragraph: The itraconazole profile compares its antifungal action with cancer-related angiogenesis and Hedgehog hypotheses.

sentences.text: The itraconazole profile compares its antifungal action with cancer-related angiogenesis and Hedgehog hypotheses.

faqs.question: Is nonsquamous disease the whole NSCLC category?
faqs.answer: No. Non-small cell lung cancer includes squamous and nonsquamous types. The itraconazole–pemetrexed study selected nonsquamous disease.

sentences.text: No. Non-small cell lung cancer includes squamous and nonsquamous types. The itraconazole–pemetrexed study selected nonsquamous disease.

guides.scope: Itraconazole added to pemetrexed in a small trial of advanced nonsquamous lung cancer.

guides.title: Breast cancer
guides.description: Metformin’s metabolic rationale and the negative disease-free-survival result of the MA.32 breast-cancer trial.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Breast cancer arises in breast tissue and includes tumors with different hormone-receptor and HER2 characteristics. Repurposing research has asked whether changing insulin and metabolism can improve outcomes alongside standard cancer care.

sentences.text: Breast cancer arises in breast tissue and includes tumors with different hormone-receptor and HER2 characteristics. Repurposing research has asked whether changing insulin and metabolism can improve outcomes alongside standard cancer care.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The large MA.32 trial did not show an invasive disease-free-survival benefit from adding metformin to standard therapy in people without diabetes who had high-risk, operable breast cancer.

sentences.text: The large MA.32 trial did not show an invasive disease-free-survival benefit from adding metformin to standard therapy in people without diabetes who had high-risk, operable breast cancer.

questions.question: Did metabolic changes translate into better cancer outcomes?
questions.answer: Metformin affected metabolic measures, including insulin-related factors, but the phase III cancer-outcome trial did not establish the hoped-for benefit.

sentences.text: Metformin affected metabolic measures, including insulin-related factors, but the phase III cancer-outcome trial did not establish the hoped-for benefit.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: MA.32 evaluated prolonged metformin exposure in people without diabetes. Metformin’s renal restrictions and gastrointestinal adverse effects remain relevant when considering prolonged additional treatment.

sentences.text: MA.32 evaluated prolonged metformin exposure in people without diabetes. Metformin’s renal restrictions and gastrointestinal adverse effects remain relevant when considering prolonged additional treatment.

sections.label: Comparisons
sections.paragraph: MA.32 compared metformin with placebo on top of standard breast-cancer treatment. Its findings do not answer whether treating diabetes with metformin should be changed in someone who also has breast cancer.

sentences.text: MA.32 compared metformin with placebo on top of standard breast-cancer treatment. Its findings do not answer whether treating diabetes with metformin should be changed in someone who also has breast cancer.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: MA.32 enrolled 3,649 participants and tested metformin over a planned five-year treatment period. Its randomized clinical endpoint is more directly informative about recurrence than earlier metabolic associations.

sentences.text: MA.32 enrolled 3,649 participants and tested metformin over a planned five-year treatment period. Its randomized clinical endpoint is more directly informative about recurrence than earlier metabolic associations.

sentences.text: The pancreatic cancer page describes a separate negative metformin trial in advanced disease; the two results should retain their different populations.

faqs.question: Does a breast-cancer diagnosis identify one tumor biology?
faqs.answer: No. Hormone receptors and HER2 status distinguish clinically important tumor groups. Findings need to be read in the population actually enrolled.

guides.title: Colorectal cancer
guides.description: Aspirin after surgery for colorectal cancers with selected PI3K-pathway alterations.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum. ALASCCA studied whether aspirin could reduce recurrence after surgery in localized cancers with selected PI3K-pathway gene alterations.

sentences.text: Colorectal cancer begins in the colon or rectum. ALASCCA studied whether aspirin could reduce recurrence after surgery in localized cancers with selected PI3K-pathway gene alterations.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: ALASCCA found fewer recurrences with aspirin in its molecularly selected population. This result applies to the tested postoperative setting and gene alterations, rather than to every colorectal cancer.

sentences.text: ALASCCA found fewer recurrences with aspirin in its molecularly selected population. This result applies to the tested postoperative setting and gene alterations, rather than to every colorectal cancer.

questions.question: How large was the recurrence difference?
questions.answer: For tumors with the prespecified PIK3CA hotspot mutations, estimated three-year recurrence was 7.7% with aspirin versus 14.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.49; 95% CI 0.24–0.98).

sentences.text: For tumors with the prespecified PIK3CA hotspot mutations, estimated three-year recurrence was 7.7% with aspirin versus 14.1% with placebo (hazard ratio 0.49; 95% CI 0.24–0.98).

sections.label: Safety

sentences.text: Severe adverse events occurred in 16.8% of the aspirin group and 11.6% of the placebo group. The benefit therefore needs to be considered alongside harm, even with a familiar medicine.

sections.label: Comparisons

sentences.text: The comparison was aspirin versus placebo after cancer treatment. It was not aspirin instead of surgery or indicated chemotherapy.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: ALASCCA used tumor PI3K-pathway alterations to define two molecular groups and followed recurrence for three years. Molecular eligibility is essential to applying its result.

sentences.text: ALASCCA used tumor PI3K-pathway alterations to define two molecular groups and followed recurrence for three years. Molecular eligibility is essential to applying its result.

sentences.text: The aspirin profile covers its established platelet action; the liver-cancer page addresses an observational prevention question rather than postoperative recurrence.

faqs.question: Why does the location of colorectal cancer matter?

guides.title: Pancreatic cancer

sections.label: Overview

sentences.text: Pancreatic cancer begins in the pancreas; the metformin trial studied advanced disease. Its purpose was to add a metabolic intervention to gemcitabine and erlotinib.

sentences.text: In a randomized trial of 121 people, adding metformin did not improve survival over placebo with the same anticancer regimen.

sentences.text: The breast cancer page describes metformin after treatment of operable cancer, a distinct setting from the advanced pancreatic trial.

faqs.question: Did the metformin trial study localized operable cancer?

guides.title: Melanoma
guides.description: Propranolol as an experimental addition to immune checkpoint treatment in melanoma.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Melanoma develops from pigment-producing melanocytes. In advanced disease, immune checkpoint drugs and, for eligible tumors, molecularly targeted treatments are important treatment approaches.

sentences.text: Melanoma develops from pigment-producing melanocytes. In advanced disease, immune checkpoint drugs and, for eligible tumors, molecularly targeted treatments are important treatment approaches.

sections.label: Options

sentences.text: A nine-person phase I study explored propranolol with pembrolizumab in advanced melanoma. It demonstrated feasibility and observed tumor responses, but had no pembrolizumab-only group to establish added benefit.

sentences.text: The trial cannot determine whether propranolol improves pembrolizumab’s response rate or survival benefit, because all participants received the combination.

guides.title: Basal-cell carcinoma
guides.description: Itraconazole in basal cell carcinoma: exploratory human tumor and pathway findings, safety signals and missing long-term outcomes.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Basal cell carcinoma begins in basal cells in the lower epidermis. It usually grows slowly but can invade surrounding tissue. Itraconazole has been studied because Hedgehog signaling is important in this cancer.

sentences.text: Basal cell carcinoma begins in basal cells in the lower epidermis. It usually grows slowly but can invade surrounding tissue. Itraconazole has been studied because Hedgehog signaling is important in this cancer.

sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Low for short-term tumor-area reduction. Nineteen of 29 enrolled participants received itraconazole in an open-label exploratory study. sections.paragraph: Multiple myeloma is a cancer of plasma cells in the bone marrow. It can damage bone and interfere with healthy blood-cell production. Experimental tumor studies and clot-prevention research answer different questions.

guides.title: Acute myeloid leukemia

questions.question: Was the favorable result in this trial due to valproate?
questions.answer: No. The factorial trial tested valproate and all-trans retinoic acid separately. Favorable remission and survival findings were associated with the retinoic-acid assignment, not valproate.

guides.title: Chronic myeloid leukemia
guides.description: Pioglitazone research aimed at deeper molecular responses in chronic myeloid leukemia.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Chronic myeloid leukemia involves abnormal myeloid blood cells. Pioglitazone has been studied alongside imatinib to target persistent leukemia cells after an initial molecular response.

sentences.text: Chronic myeloid leukemia involves abnormal myeloid blood cells. Pioglitazone has been studied alongside imatinib to target persistent leukemia cells after an initial molecular response.

sections.label: Options
sections.paragraph: The ACTIM study reported deep molecular responses after adding pioglitazone to imatinib. Its single-arm design cannot establish how many responses were caused by pioglitazone rather than continued imatinib treatment. ACTIM enrolled people whose CML was already responding to long-term imatinib, but had not reached the study's deeper molecular-response target. It therefore examined an add-on strategy for residual disease, rather than pioglitazone as a replacement for a leukemia medicine. Twenty-four patients were evaluable. The estimated cumulative incidence of reaching MR4.5 by 12 months was 56%, with a 95% confidence interval of 37% to 76%.

sentences.text: The ACTIM study reported deep molecular responses after adding pioglitazone to imatinib. Its single-arm design cannot establish how many responses were caused by pioglitazone rather than continued imatinib treatment.

questions.question: Was pioglitazone tested instead of imatinib?
questions.answer: No. Participants continued imatinib, and the question was whether adding pioglitazone could deepen an existing molecular response.

sentences.text: No. Participants continued imatinib, and the question was whether adding pioglitazone could deepen an existing molecular response.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: Edema led one ACTIM participant to stop pioglitazone. Fluid retention is especially relevant when adding this medicine to an ongoing cancer regimen. The main report also describes weight gain and a reduction in hemoglobin during treatment. Pioglitazone exposure varied because several participants stopped early after a regulatory concern about bladder cancer; the study was too small to resolve uncommon or delayed harms. These observations qualify the interpretation of tolerability and do not establish the safety of adding pioglitazone to every CML regimen.

sections.paragraph: ACTIM did not include a randomized imatinib-only group. Historical response rates offer context but cannot provide an equally reliable treatment comparison.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: ACTIM used a molecular endpoint, MR4.5, indicating very low BCR::ABL1 transcript levels. The absence of concurrent randomization limits attribution of deeper response. Confidence that pioglitazone itself improves CML outcomes is Low. A separate imatinib-only cohort provided a nonrandomized comparison, so differences between patients or continued imatinib treatment could help explain the apparent response. MR4.5 describes a very low level of leukemia-associated RNA; it is not the same as a demonstrated survival advantage, cure or evidence that stopping imatinib is safe. The authors called for confirmation in a randomized trial.

faqs.answer: The test measures BCR::ABL1 transcripts. MR4.5 indicates a very deep reduction, and is different from an ordinary blood count becoming normal.

The mechanism remains a rationale for investigation. Its relationship to a patient-important treatment benefit has Low clinical confidence in this single-arm study.

guides.title: Parkinson disease

sections.paragraph: Parkinson’s disease affects movement and many nonmotor functions. Loss of dopamine-producing neurons contributes to slowness, stiffness and tremor; levodopa helps movement symptoms but does not replace lost neurons.

sentences.text: Parkinson’s disease affects movement and many nonmotor functions. Loss of dopamine-producing neurons contributes to slowness, stiffness and tremor; levodopa helps movement symptoms but does not replace lost neurons.

sentences.text: Vitiligo causes loss of pigment when melanocytes are destroyed or stop functioning. Autoimmune processes are important in the disease, and visible skin changes can substantially affect quality of life.

guides.title: Sarcopenia
guides.description: Metformin studies of walking speed and muscle adaptation in older adults.

sections.paragraph: Sarcopenia involves declining muscle strength and function, often with reduced muscle mass. Difficulty rising from a chair, slower walking and increased falls can threaten independence. Resistance activity and adequate nutrition are central to preserving muscle health.

sentences.text: Sarcopenia involves declining muscle strength and function, often with reduced muscle mass. Difficulty rising from a chair, slower walking and increased falls can threaten independence. Resistance activity and adequate nutrition are central to preserving muscle health.

sentences.text: Metformin did not improve walking speed in MET-PREVENT. A separate resistance-training trial found smaller gains in muscle size with metformin, challenging the idea that a diabetes drug necessarily improves muscle aging.

guides.title: Drug repurposing
guides.description: How existing medicines become candidates for new uses, and how mechanisms, clinical evidence and approval fit together.
guides.scope: How existing medicines become candidates for new uses, and how mechanisms, clinical evidence and approval fit together.

sections.label: Overview
sections.title: Overview
sections.paragraph: Drug repurposing investigates whether an existing medicine or investigational compound can treat a different condition. The starting point is prior knowledge about the compound; the new use remains a question to test.

sentences.text: Drug repurposing investigates whether an existing medicine or investigational compound can treat a different condition.
The starting point is prior knowledge about the compound; the new use remains a question to test.

sections.label: Rationale
sections.title: Why repurpose a drug?
sections.paragraph: Existing compounds may already have manufacturing, laboratory and human data, allowing researchers to build on earlier development. That can shorten some development steps, although a new indication still needs evidence and may face funding barriers, especially for off-patent medicines.

sentences.text: Existing compounds may already have manufacturing, laboratory and human data, allowing researchers to build on earlier development.
That can shorten some development steps, although a new indication still needs evidence and may face funding barriers, especially for off-patent medicines.

sections.label: Mechanisms
sections.title: Mechanisms
sections.paragraph: A mechanism of action describes the biological steps through which a drug acts. Researchers can look for a relevant target or disease process, screen compounds, and confirm activity in cells or animals before clinical testing. Examples of biological questions include effects on the Hedgehog pathway, apoptosis, autophagy or angiogenesis. Each names a process to investigate, not a promise that changing it will improve a disease.

sentences.text: A mechanism of action describes the biological steps through which a drug acts. Researchers can look for a relevant target or disease process, screen compounds, and confirm activity in cells or animals before clinical testing.

Examples of biological questions include effects on the Hedgehog pathway, apoptosis, autophagy or angiogenesis. Each names a process to investigate, not a promise that changing it will improve a disease.

sections.label: Evidence
sections.title: Evidence
sections.paragraph: Basic research tests biological ideas; translational research develops them toward possible interventions; clinical trials evaluate effects in people. Controlled trials compare a treatment group with standard care or an inactive control, helping distinguish treatment effects from what would otherwise happen. For a repurposing claim, read the population, treatment, comparison and measured outcome together. A laboratory pathway change answers a different question from improved symptoms or survival.

sentences.text: Basic research tests biological ideas; translational research develops them toward possible interventions; clinical trials evaluate effects in people.
Controlled trials compare a treatment group with standard care or an inactive control, helping distinguish treatment effects from what would otherwise happen.
For a repurposing claim, read the population, treatment, comparison and measured outcome together. A laboratory pathway change answers a different question from improved symptoms or survival.

sections.label: Status
sections.title: Approval and off-label use
sections.paragraph: Off-label use means prescribing an approved drug outside its approved indication, route or dose. In the United States, clinicians may do this when medically appropriate, but FDA has not determined safety and effectiveness for that unapproved use. Repurposing is the research and development question; off-label use is a prescribing status. A successful repurposing program can seek a new approved indication.

sentences.text: Off-label use means prescribing an approved drug outside its approved indication, route or dose. In the United States, clinicians may do this when medically appropriate, but FDA has not determined safety and effectiveness for that unapproved use.
Repurposing is the research and development question; off-label use is a prescribing status. A successful repurposing program can seek a new approved indication.

sections.label: Safety
sections.title: Safety
sections.paragraph: Approval for one use does not mean a medicine is free of risks. The intended condition, dose and route matter when weighing benefits and harms. Metformin’s established role in type 2 diabetes, for example, does not remove its kidney-related restrictions or lactic-acidosis warning.

sentences.text: Approval for one use does not mean a medicine is free of risks. The intended condition, dose and route matter when weighing benefits and harms.
