sections.label: Reading
sections.title: Reading a repurposing claim
sections.paragraph: Ask what the medicine is already approved for, what studies support the proposed use, how it compares with available treatments, and what harms are possible. Then examine study design and outcomes: an experimental result is most useful when the comparison and the question it answers are clear.

sentences.text: Ask what the medicine is already approved for, what studies support the proposed use, how it compares with available treatments, and what harms are possible.
Then examine study design and outcomes: an experimental result is most useful when the comparison and the question it answers are clear.

faqs.answer: No. FDA approval concerns specified uses; a different indication needs its own assessment of safety and effectiveness.

sentences.text: No. FDA approval concerns specified uses; a different indication needs its own assessment of safety and effectiveness.

faqs.question: Why include mechanisms when clinical outcomes matter?
faqs.answer: Mechanisms help formulate and test a rationale. Clinical studies then assess whether that rationale translates into useful effects in people.

sentences.text: Mechanisms help formulate and test a rationale. Clinical studies then assess whether that rationale translates into useful effects in people.

guides.title: Type 2 diabetes

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Type 2 diabetes is a condition in which blood glucose remains too high because tissues do not respond adequately to insulin and the pancreas cannot supply enough insulin to compensate. Over time, diabetes can damage the eyes, kidneys, nerves and cardiovascular system.

sections.label: Options

sentences.text: Management combines healthy daily habits, monitoring and medicines selected for the person’s glucose levels and other health conditions.

guides.title: Fluconazole

sections.paragraph: Fluconazole is a triazole antifungal medicine used for susceptible fungal infections, including Candida infections and fungal meningitis. It slows fungal growth; its established infection uses do not establish benefit for unrelated diseases.

guides.description: What drug studies tell us about lifespan, physical function and other outcomes of aging.

sections.label: Options

questions.question: Does metformin improve muscle function with age?

sections.label: Evidence
sections.paragraph: PEARL analyzed 114 completers after 48 weeks and found no significant difference in visceral adiposity, its primary outcome. The mouse lifespan experiments are direct survival tests in mice. Translating that result to human lifespan requires a different kind and duration of study.

guides.title: Methylene blue
guides.description: A dye-based medicine studied as an add-on in septic shock, as a disc injection for low back pain and with light for toenail fungus.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Methylene blue is a dye that is also used as a medicine. The open-access studies on file cover three off-label uses: an add-on treatment in septic shock, injection into a painful spinal disc, and photodynamic therapy for toenail fungus. One child case report describes its use to prevent ifosfamide-related brain toxicity.

sentences.text: Methylene blue is a dye that is also used as a medicine.
The open-access studies on file cover three off-label uses: an add-on treatment in septic shock, injection into a painful spinal disc, and photodynamic therapy for toenail fungus.
One child case report describes its use to prevent ifosfamide-related brain toxicity.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Moderate for one outcome, from one single-center trial. In 91 adults with septic shock, methylene blue started within 24 hours shortened time to vasopressor discontinuation (69 versus 94 hours) and added about one vasopressor-free day by day 28. Mortality and days on a ventilator were similar between groups. Clinical evidence: Low. In an uncontrolled study of 20 adults, pain scores fell at 3 months after one intradiscal injection, but by 12 months average pain was no different from before treatment, and 5 of 20 patients (20%) kept a successful result. Clinical evidence: Low. Small studies without an untreated or standard-drug control used methylene blue with red light (photodynamic therapy) for toenail fungus. In 22 patients, clinical response was 100% in mild-to-moderate disease and 63.6% in severe disease. In a 20-toenail randomized comparison of two pretreatments, mycological cure at 40 weeks was 70% after urea and 40% after laser.

sections.paragraph: In the septic shock trial, the authors reported no serious adverse effects related to methylene blue. No side effects were detected in the 20-toenail photodynamic therapy study. These are small studies and cannot rule out uncommon harms.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.paragraph: Doses differ by use and are not interchangeable. In the septic shock trial, the median daily dose was 1.2 mg/kg. Each dose in the septic shock trial was 100 mg of methylene blue in 500 ml of 0.9% sodium chloride solution over 6 hours once daily for a total of 3 doses, with no bolus; the authors report a cumulative dose of 3.6 mg/kg over 54 hours. The control group received the same schedule of 500 ml of 0.9% sodium chloride without methylene blue, and the infusion was started on average 8.3 hours (methylene blue group) and 7.6 hours (control group) after shock was identified. The planned multicenter trial in refractory septic shock specifies a 2 mg/kg methylene blue bolus over 20 minutes, then 0.5 mg/kg/h continuously for 48 hours, against 50 mL of 5% glucose solution as placebo; it enrolls adults needing norepinephrine of at least 0.5 mcg/kg/min or an equivalent, and its primary outcome is total vasopressor dose over the first 48 hours. In the uncontrolled back pain study, each target disc received 1 ml of methylene blue and 1 ml of 2% lidocaine hydrochloride by a double-needle technique under fluoroscopy, 7 days after provocative discography; the article does not state the methylene blue concentration. Pain (VAS) and disability (ODI) were assessed at baseline and at 1, 3, 6 and 12 months, and success was defined as a VAS reduction of at least 2 points. The planned randomized trial gives 1 ml of methylene blue (10 mg methylthioninium) with 0.5 ml of 2% lidocaine hydrochloride and 0.5 ml of contrast, against 1 ml of isotonic saline with the same lidocaine and contrast, at a maximum pressure of 100 PSI and 0.02 ml/s, with follow-up at 6 weeks and 3, 6, 12 and 24 months. The 22-patient toenail study applied a 2% aqueous methylene blue solution followed by red light at 630 nm and 36 J/cm2, with a 15-day interval between sessions for 6 months; the article gives no incubation time. The toenail studies applied a 2% methylene blue solution to the nail and then red light at 630 nm, every two weeks for six months. In the randomized pretreatment comparison, 2% methylene blue was left on the nail for 3 minutes before a red LED lamp at 635 nm (fluence 37 J/cm2, irradiance 70 mW/cm2, 10 minutes of exposure), for 9 sessions 2 weeks apart over 16 weeks; one group used 40% urea ointment under an occlusive dressing for 12 hours at night beforehand, and the other used a fractional Er:YAG laser at 2940 nm. Disc injection was done once, into discs confirmed by provocative discography.

guides.title: Melphalan
guides.description: A chemotherapy agent given to the liver in uveal melanoma, by mouth in myeloma combinations and in high-dose regimens before stem cell transplantation.

sections.label: Overview
sections.paragraph: Melphalan is an alkylating chemotherapy agent used in conditioning regimens before stem cell transplantation. The open-access studies on file cover its use delivered directly to the liver in uveal melanoma, by mouth with bortezomib and prednisone in multiple myeloma, and inside high-dose regimens for lymphoma. Regional therapies for limb tumors have almost all used melphalan with circulatory isolation.

sentences.text: Melphalan is an alkylating chemotherapy agent used in conditioning regimens before stem cell transplantation.

The open-access studies on file cover its use delivered directly to the liver in uveal melanoma, by mouth with bortezomib and prednisone in multiple myeloma, and inside high-dose regimens for lymphoma.
Regional therapies for limb tumors have almost all used melphalan with circulatory isolation.

sections.label: Benefits
sections.paragraph: Clinical evidence: Moderate for progression-free survival, from one phase III randomized trial. In the SCANDIUM trial of 87 patients with uveal melanoma liver metastases, isolated hepatic perfusion with melphalan gave median progression-free survival of 7.4 versus 3.3 months (hazard ratio 0.21; 95% CI, 0.12-0.36), but the primary endpoint of 24-month overall survival (46.5% versus 29.5%, P = 0.12) was not met. Clinical evidence: Low to moderate. In the FOCUS study of Melphalan/Hepatic Delivery System, the study design was amended to a single-arm study and the randomized efficacy analyses were exploratory. Median overall survival was 18.5 versus 14.5 months and median progression-free survival 9.1 versus 3.3 months against best alternative care, with numerical differences only. Clinical evidence: Moderate for the myeloma combination, from a phase 3 trial. In the final OCTANS analysis, the daratumumab, bortezomib, melphalan and prednisone combination (D-VMP) had median progression-free survival of 38.7 versus 19.2 months with bortezomib, melphalan and prednisone (VMP) alone. The benefit is reported for the daratumumab combination, not for melphalan on its own. Clinical evidence: Low. Adding oncolytic virus T-VEC to melphalan and tumor necrosis factor by isolated limb perfusion gave an overall response rate of 53% in a first-in-human trial.

sections.label: Safety
sections.paragraph: In the FOCUS study, serious adverse events occurred in 51.2% of Melphalan/HDS patients and 21.9% of best alternative care patients. The most common were thrombocytopenia (19.5%), neutropenia (9.8%), leukopenia (9.8%) and febrile neutropenia (7.3%). No treatment-related deaths were observed. In the subgroup analyses the safety profile was similar across subgroups, without evidence of cumulative toxicity with successive treatment cycles. In the HAITILS trial all six patients (100%) had grade 3 or higher hematologic adverse events related to melphalan preconditioning. In a randomized trial of 86 patients receiving melphalan before autologous stem cell transplantation, grade III-IV oral mucositis occurred in 32.5% of the control group (saline ice cubes) and 10.8% of the Kangfuxin ice cube group. Adding brentuximab vedotin to the melphalan-containing BeEAM regimen may increase pulmonary toxicity: two patients in the brentuximab arm developed grade 3 pneumonitis. In a pooled analysis of MAIA and ALCYONE, grade 3/4 infections were 36.9% with daratumumab combinations versus 22.4% without. Melphalan was part of the ALCYONE regimens only, so this difference is not attributed to melphalan.

sections.label: Dosing
sections.paragraph: Doses differ by use and are not interchangeable. Melphalan/Hepatic Delivery System was given at 3 mg/kg ideal body weight once every 6 to 8 weeks for a maximum of 6 cycles. In the OCTANS regimen, melphalan was given by mouth at 9 mg/m2 on Days 1-4 of each 42-day cycle, for up to nine cycles, with bortezomib and prednisone. In the HAITILS trial, melphalan 1 mg/kg was given intravenously on day -5 as preconditioning before cell infusion. In the BeEAM regimen, melphalan 140 mg/m2 was given as a single infusion over 60 minutes on day -1. In 20 children, population modeling estimated melphalan clearance at 24.9 L/h normalized to a body weight of 28 kg, and concomitant busulfan was associated with about 18% higher exposure.

sections.label: Results
sections.paragraph: In the SCANDIUM trial, median overall survival was 21.7 versus 17.6 months (hazard ratio 0.64; 95% CI, 0.37-1.10), and quality of life measured by EQ-5D-3L stayed high in the perfusion group over 12 months while trending down in the control group. In the FOCUS study, exploratory objective response rate was 27.5% versus 9.4% and disease control rate 80.0% versus 46.9% for Melphalan/HDS versus best alternative care. In the FOCUS subgroup analyses, patients with lower tumor burden had better objective response rate (51.1% versus 22.2%), median progression-free survival (11.3 versus 5.8 months) and median overall survival (26.7 versus 15.4 months) than those with higher tumor burden. In OCTANS, the rate of very good partial response or better was 80.1% with D-VMP versus 47.3% with VMP, and minimal residual disease negativity was 40.4% versus 10.8%. Patient-reported outcomes in OCTANS improved in both arms, with significantly larger improvements with D-VMP in global health status at 9 months and in social functioning and nausea and vomiting scores at 12 months. Adding brentuximab vedotin to BeEAM did not change response rate, disease-free survival or overall survival in 25 patients, and the study stopped early after a futility analysis. In the HAITILS trial, best overall response was stable disease in all six patients, with median progression-free survival of 4 months and median overall survival of 14 months.

The regional-therapy field is testing combinations, including T-VEC with melphalan by limb perfusion and a different intra-arterial drug, CBL0137, in small early-phase studies.

Lymphoma, pediatric pharmacokinetic, mucositis, cell therapy and limb perfusion reports are small or secondary studies.

glossary.title: Relative risk
glossary.meaning: The risk of an event in one group divided by the risk of that event in a comparison group.
glossary.context: Also called a risk ratio. The same relative difference can accompany different absolute risks, so the event, population and follow-up must stay visible.
glossary.examples: For an illustrative calculation only, risks of 2% and 4% give a risk ratio of 0.5 and an absolute difference of 2 percentage points. These are teaching numbers, not study findings.

glossary.title: Off-label use
glossary.meaning: Use of an approved drug in a way not included in its approved labeling.
glossary.context: The FDA explains that this can involve a different condition, route or dose. It does not mean that the FDA has established safety and effectiveness for that unapproved use.
glossary.examples: A regulatory assessment must name the product, jurisdiction, indication and date. This glossary definition does not establish the current status of any specific drug–long-COVID use.

glossary.title: Hedgehog pathway
glossary.meaning: The Hedgehog pathway is a cell-signaling system that carries messages from the cell surface to the nucleus and helps regulate growth and development.
glossary.context: Hedgehog pathway inhibition means reduced activity of this cell-signaling system in a specified assay or tissue. A drug's established antifungal action does not prove that it inhibits Hedgehog signaling, and a biomarker change does not by itself establish a clinical cancer benefit.
glossary.examples: A Hedgehog inhibitor targets this signaling route. Whether a particular drug helps a particular cancer still requires clinical testing.

glossary.title: Cholesterol transport inhibition
glossary.meaning: Cholesterol transport inhibition means interfering with the movement of cholesterol between cellular locations.
glossary.context: NPC1 is one protein involved in moving cholesterol and other lipids within cells; impaired function can trap lipids in the wrong compartments.
glossary.examples: A study of intracellular cholesterol transport asks a different question from a blood cholesterol test. Disrupted transport can damage cells, so inhibition is not inherently beneficial.

glossary.title: Apoptosis
glossary.meaning: Apoptosis is a controlled sequence of events that ends in a cell’s death, often called programmed cell death.
glossary.context: It helps remove cells that are abnormal or no longer needed, and some cancer cells evade it.
glossary.examples: Showing apoptosis in cancer cells is a mechanistic observation; a patient trial is needed to determine whether a treatment improves health.

glossary.title: Autophagy
glossary.meaning: Autophagy is cellular breakdown and recycling of proteins and other internal material, including damaged components.
glossary.context: Its effects depend on context: recycling can protect normal cells, but established cancer cells may also use it to survive stress.
glossary.examples: An increase in autophagy should therefore be interpreted alongside the disease model and outcome, rather than treated as an automatic health benefit.

glossary.title: Biofilm
glossary.meaning: A biofilm is a community of microbes embedded in a surrounding matrix that the microbes produce.
glossary.context: Biofilms can contain bacteria or fungi and occur on body surfaces, such as teeth, as well as on objects.
glossary.examples: Preventing a biofilm from forming and disrupting an existing biofilm are distinct experimental questions; neither alone establishes a clinical treatment benefit.

glossary.title: Candida albicans
glossary.meaning: Candida albicans is one species of Candida, a group of yeasts that can live on the body without causing symptoms.
glossary.context: Candida overgrowth can cause candidiasis; infection severity depends on the body site and the person’s risk factors.
glossary.examples: Finding Candida without symptoms does not by itself establish vaginal infection or a need for antifungal treatment.

glossary.title: Hyphae
glossary.meaning: Hyphae are microscopic fungal filaments; a network of these filaments forms a mycelium.
glossary.context: Candida yeast-to-hypha morphogenesis is the transition from budding yeast to filamentous growth. Inhibiting new hyphal formation, killing existing filaments and clearing an infection in a patient are different outcomes.
glossary.examples: A change in fungal shape is a different observation from symptom resolution or clearance of infection in a patient.

glossary.title: Angiogenesis
glossary.meaning: Angiogenesis is the formation of blood vessels.
glossary.context: Tumors can stimulate nearby cells and tissues to grow vessels that support further tumor growth.
glossary.examples: Anti-angiogenic activity describes an effect on vessel formation; it does not by itself quantify a survival benefit.

glossary.title: Hypoxia
glossary.meaning: Hypoxia means that a tissue has a reduced supply of oxygen.
glossary.context: In a tumor, the degree of hypoxia can influence how the tumor responds to treatment.
glossary.examples: Measuring oxygen in the relevant tissue addresses hypoxia more directly than assuming that a change in blood flow corrected it.

glossary.title: Oxygenation
glossary.meaning: Oxygenation describes oxygen reaching blood or tissue; inhaled oxygen normally moves from the lungs into blood and then to tissues.
glossary.context: Local oxygenation concerns a particular tissue, while hypoxia describes an inadequate oxygen supply there.
glossary.examples: A claim of increased local oxygenation needs a measurement in the relevant tissue, rather than a blood-flow change alone.

glossary.title: mTOR
glossary.meaning: mTOR, the mechanistic target of rapamycin, is a protein kinase involved in cell growth, division and survival.
glossary.context: Some cancer cells have increased mTOR activity, making this pathway a target for treatment research.
glossary.examples: Rapamycin is another name for sirolimus. Its interaction with mTOR explains a biological target, while clinical effects depend on the condition and treatment tested.

glossary.title: PDE5
glossary.meaning: Phosphodiesterase type 5, or PDE5, is an enzyme that breaks down cyclic GMP, a signal involved in smooth-muscle relaxation.
glossary.context: PDE5 inhibition preserves this signal and can increase blood flow in responsive tissues.
glossary.examples: Tadalafil inhibits PDE5, but its erectile effect still requires sexual stimulation to trigger nitric-oxide signaling.

glossary.title: Ergosterol
glossary.meaning: Ergosterol is a steroid found in fungi and is part of the sterol pathway targeted by azole antifungals.
glossary.context: Fluconazole inhibits the fungal enzyme lanosterol 14-alpha-demethylase, reducing the conversion of lanosterol toward ergosterol.
glossary.examples: This fungal sterol mechanism is distinct from inhibiting cholesterol transport inside human cells.
